title: Ang 705–710: Jaitsri ki Var
tomorrow: what do you say to someone you're about to miss?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Jaitsri: a Guru remembered for courage writes that fear came in, and takes it to shelter. Quiet strength. Today that strength gets a ballad.

Stadium chants, a walk-out song, the anthem before the game: people sing about strength. In Punjabi, a var is a ballad, a form known for songs of heroes. On ang 705 Guru Arjan writes one, Jaitsri ki Var, and the hero isn't a warrior at all. It opens: perfect at the beginning, perfect in the middle, perfect at the end, the Lord of all.
screen: `A WALK-OUT SONG.` → `A VAR: A BALLAD OF HEROES.` → `PERFECT AT THE BEGINNING.`

segments.voice: A var moves in steps. Each stanza is a pauri, a step on a stair, and in the Granth short saloks often come before it. Guru Arjan keeps that shape and turns it toward God. The opening salok, in paraphrase: perfect at the beginning, in the middle and at the end; the saints remember the One who is everywhere; Nanak says, the Lord of the world destroys sin. Listen to the strength in that. It isn't one big moment of winning. It's a line that holds from first to last, steady as a beat you could tap. Then, after the ballad, one hymn by Ravidas, on ang 710, and it sounds like the opposite. In paraphrase: Lord, I know nothing. My mind has been sold into the world's hands. Put the two side by side and they fit. The ballad says the strength runs from beginning to end, and it isn't ours to supply. Ravidas says honestly: I can't hold this up by myself. The hero's song and the humble confession meet in one place. The hero of this ballad doesn't flex. Its strength is that the beat never drops. Strength.
screen: `A VAR CLIMBS IN STEPS.` · `BEGINNING, MIDDLE, END.` · `RAVIDAS: I KNOW NOTHING.` · `THE BEAT NEVER DROPS.` · then, large: `STRENGTH.`

segments.voice: Tap a slow, steady beat on your knee with one hand, and let your breath find it: in on one tap, out on the next. Partway through, let the hand go still and keep listening for the beat that's still there, your breath, your pulse. Beginning, middle, end.
Ang 705. Where Guru Arjan's ballad in Jaitsri begins: perfect at the beginning, in the middle and at the end.
Strength: the beat that holds from the first line to the last, even when you know nothing. Fifteen-thirty, in rhythm.

chat.says: dad's doing all the wedding setup alone, says he's strong enough. he's wiped. how do i tell him?
options: Tell him the ballad's strength runs start to finish, and it isn't his alone.
Let him be. Real strength means handling all of it without any help.
Tell him strong people don't get tired, so he must be doing it wrong.
chat.meaning: Guru Arjan's ballad puts the strength in the One present at the beginning, middle and end; Ravidas admits he can't hold it up alone.

pauri.meaning: a stanza of a var; literally a step

salok.meaning: a short verse, often set before a pauri
